en: Using a movable pulley cuts the required lifting force in half, but you must pull the rope twice as far.
A wheelbarrow acts as a second-class lever because the heavy load is positioned between the wheel fulcrum and your lifting hands.
Teflon has such incredibly low friction that almost nothing can stick to it, making it perfect for non-stick frying pans.
A parachute uses air friction, also called drag, to slow a skydiver's fall to a safe landing speed.
If you weigh 100 pounds on Earth, you would only weigh about 16.5 pounds on the Moon.
A tightrope walker carries a long, heavy pole to lower their center of gravity and maintain perfect balance.
The magnetic north pole that attracts a compass needle is actually a magnetic south pole located near the geographic North Pole.
A stretched rubber band stores elastic potential energy, which instantly transforms into kinetic energy the moment you let it go.
A single bolt of lightning can heat the surrounding air to 30,000 degrees Celsius, which is five times hotter than the Sun's surface.
Light travels so incredibly fast that it can circle the Earth's equator about seven and a half times in just one second.
Sound travels more than four times faster in water than in air because water molecules are packed much closer together.
A thermos flask keeps liquids hot by using a vacuum layer between its walls to completely stop heat conduction and convection.
